name: Le Méridien Grand Hotel Nuremberg
positioning: Historic grand hotel opposite Nuremberg central station at the entrance to the old town, with a protected Belle Epoque ballroom
best_for: Travelers who want a central base by the station and the old town
Art and history lovers drawn to the hotel's heritage and the nearby Neues Museum
Guests before or after a Main-Danube river cruise

facts.text: The hotel is centrally located opposite Nuremberg central station and at the entrance of the historical old town.
The underground is right outside the door.
The building was originally a two-storey farmhouse with a hops storehouse.
Famous guests who have stayed at the hotel include the Dalai Lama, Robbie Williams and The Beatles.
The Albrecht-Duerer-Saal is decorated in Art Deco style and lit through a glass roof.
Rooms have the Le Méridien Bed, designed by LM 100 artist Nick Dine.
Rooms look out over the courtyard, the historic train station or the Old Quarter.
The Neues Museum's contemporary art scene is a few minutes' walk from the hotel.
Restaurant Brasserie has a show kitchen and serves regional specialties such as Nuremberg bratwurst.
The Atelier Bar serves specialty cocktails and drinks.
The gym has cardio equipment and a sauna.
Trained pets are welcome to join guests on their stay.

highlights.text: The mirrored, chandeliered Belle Epoque ballroom is a protected monument, decorated with motifs from Richard Wagner's operas.
Guests find a complimentary admission ticket to Nuremberg's Neues Museum in their room.
Rooms feature Art Nouveau-inspired marble bathrooms and contemporary artworks.
The hotel hosts a Musical Dinner Show and a Murder Mystery Dinner.
The hotel is near the Nuremberg River Cruise Port, a convenient stay before or after a cruise on the Main-Danube Canal.

considerations.text: Rooms do not have a fridge.
Guests must be at least 18 years old to check in.
